authorised_by: owner instruction pasted-text-2026-10-10T08-54-57.txt, section 1 (provisional tolerances 1e-5 A for RMSD, 1e-7 for DockQ)
frozen_before: any v0.1.1 test run on any platform, and before the new AlphaFold 3 / Chai-1 / RF2NA fixtures were selected
does_not_change: the v0.1.0.dev0 macOS self-test result, which FAILED under its predeclared 1e-6 bound and remains recorded as FAIL (qualification_v0.1.0.dev0/selftest_record_macos_arm64.json)

reference.applies_to: the reference platform (karyon: Linux x86-64, the platform that produced the frozen values)
reference.rule: every compared value bit-identical (==), including unrounded floats

portable.rule: exact (==) for everything except the floating-point quantities listed in `tolerances`; each listed quantity within its absolute tolerance; every deviation reported, including those within tolerance

rmsd_angstrom.justification: owner-specified 1e-5 A; observed v0.1.0.dev0 macOS maxima 4.5e-6 A (LRMSD), 1.8e-7 A (iRMSD), 7e-15 A (geometry)

no_additional_float_tolerances: No other floating-point quantity receives a tolerance. fnat and fnonnat are ratios of integer contact counts that are themselves required to be exact, so they are compared exactly; any floating-point quantity not listed above is compared exactly.
always_exact: reported (displayed) values: DockQ, fnat, iRMSD, LRMSD to 3 decimals and geometry RMSDs to 2 decimals, compared as the formatted strings shown in summary.txt
DockQ threshold class (incorrect/acceptable/medium/high) computed from the unrounded value
status, failure stage, failure / NO_VALUE reason, geometry exclusion
selected chain mapping, number of admissible candidates, number of interfaces
residue correspondence counts (in frame / out of frame / indeterminate)
all integer counts (contacts, residue lengths, aligned pairs)
output identity: prediction and reference SHA-256
failure_handling: If the portable qualification fails under this profile, the result is reported as FAIL and work stops for review. Tolerances are not widened after seeing results.
